correctness.rationale: For real |lambda|<1/2 the two boundary binomial series converge absolutely on every smaller parameter interval. Since H is inner, for j>k the (j,k) moment is the constant Fourier term of (1+z)^j H^(j-k) (1+z^(-1))^k and only uses the Taylor jet through k. The j=k moment is independent of H, and swapping j,k conjugates the result. The two Blaschke products agree through degree M-1; at total order at most 2M every unequal pair has smaller index at most M-1. At total order 2M+1 only (M+1,M) and its reversal see the coefficient of degree M, and its multiplier in the nonconjugated integral is exactly 1. The real coefficient difference there is -(1-a^2), giving -2(1-a^2) beta_M beta_(M+1), which cannot vanish when p/2 is nonintegral and 0<a<1. Taking M above any requested jet length proves the claim for each d>=1, since the probe has degree one. No optimization argument is used, including for 0<p<=1. The supplied script and stored 72-case exact output were inspected, not rerun; they illustrate the proof, which establishes the universal claim.
